For those that does not have a NAS drive yet:

  • A NAS drive does not substitute for a backup. NAS drives can sometimes crash or goes berserk and corrupt your data. So still need an external hard disk backup.
  • NAS drives can be hacked or infected by cryptoware.
  • The hard disk in the NAS drives must be NAS drive certified. Other hard disks will work too but NAS aware hard disks take vibration of the other hard disks into account because they are closely packed and affects each other.
  • The NAS drives works optimal if it has 30% space left. It gets below that threshold, then add another disk.
  • Use an UPS to prevent accidental power outage.
  • It uses Linux, so make sure that you have a bit of knowledge of Linux.

Originally I had external hard disks and a backup plan. Until a point where I discovered that my hard disk was failing (behind my back and Windows did not tell me this). So the data became silently corrupt. I had tens of thousand of photos and images and they all silently started to become corrupt. (Data rot)

All my backups started to become corrupt and I did not know.

One day massive hard disk failure, and I almost lost everything. This tool actually saved me in time: http://www.hdsentinel.com/ Windows did not know that my hard disk were failing. And when I tried a new hard disk to restore the backed up data and realized that they had been, corrupt for months. So I did not have any backup anymore.

The hard disk did not fail yet but it took days to copy data from it. I did lose photos but in the end 98% got saved before it completely died.

Now that I have everything saved on the NAS drive, I can tell it to backup to yet another external hard disk from time to time. When a NAS fails (the Linux crashes) your data on the disks basically are lost. But because it copied them to an external hard disk, I can mount the external hard disk in Windows again.

The most interesting thing about a NAS is that it can test your drives and SCRUB the hard disk. This basically checks every bit on your NAS drives for bit rot. Data silently being corrupted. And it all happens without you to wait until teh job completed. The NAS drive works day and night, even the backup to an external hard disk is done automatically.

Before I had the NAS drive, a full backup could take 25 hours, so I postponed full backups more and more. But with the NAS drive, I backup every time I added something important on it. Then let it automatically do its thing.

So I have similar problems. The big question is what is your drop number (the difference between your chest/shoulder measurement and your waist? Most American suits now are cut for Drop 5 (So a 42 inch chest - jacket is cut for a 37 inch waist - OBEAST HO!) If you are anywhere from a drop 6-8 you should be able to tailor. If you are a drop 9-10 you can try tailoring, but don't buy anything patterned cause they will have to take so much fabric out of it it'll look weird to the discerning eye. If you are drop 11+ you are probably screwed and will need at the least made to measure. Indochino has some decently priced made to measure for what it is.
